### Observed differences

- The block A19–A20–A25 ran in every trace in the earlier window (200 of 200, about once per trace); in the later window each of the three runs in only about 53 in 100 traces (106–108 of 200), still about once per trace when present. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007]
- A direct step from A41 to A26 appears: before, about 96 in 100 of A41's outgoing transitions went to A19 and none went to A26; in the later window about 47 in 100 go to A19 and 39 in 100 go straight to A26, and A41→A26 pairs at the shortest gap rise from 0 to about 48 in 100 (about 200 transitions and pairs behind each window). [DIR008, LAG008]
- The block is skipped rather than rerouted: A20 still leads to A26 in about 97 in 100 of its transitions in both windows; A15→A26 within five steps, seen in only 1 trace before, appears in 75 traces; and A14→A41 pairs at the larger gap fall from 71 to 33 in 100. [DIR007, LAG007, LAG005]
- A06 loses its place between A14 and A15: before, A06 ran in 71 in 100 traces, A14 led to A06 in 69 in 100 of its outgoing transitions and A06 led to A15 in 92 in 100; in the later window A14 leads straight to A15 in 78 in 100 (A06 only 12 in 100), A06 runs in 26 in 100 traces, the A14→A15 gap shortens (shortest-gap share 17→41 in 100) and A14→A06 shortest-gap pairs fall from 98 to 75 in 100 on far fewer pairs (140→32). [OCC002, DIR005, DIR003, LAG003, LAG004]
- A06's remaining occurrences look different: its outgoing transitions are spread (A15 37, A45 12, A26 11, A47 8 in 100) instead of concentrated on A15 (92 in 100), and it sits later in the trace (median relative position 0.16→0.30, upper quartile 0.17→0.83). [DIR003, POS001]
- Three rare activities participate more often (A04 5→15, A08 4→20, A10 5→16 in 100 traces); A44→A45 and A46→A47 become slightly less exclusive (96→86 and 97→87 in 100 of transitions); the outgoing profiles of the rare activities A02, A04 and A08 are redistributed, though on only about 8–43 observed transitions per window. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, DIR009, DIR010, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, previously mandatory parts of the process are skipped in a large share of cases: A14 goes straight to A15, bypassing A06 (participation 71→26 in 100 traces), and A41 goes straight to A26, bypassing the block A19–A20–A25 (each from 100 to about 53 in 100 traces). The signs are direct and consistent: the successor shifts at A14 and A41 rest on about 200 outgoing transitions in each window; the A41→A26 shortest-gap share rises from 0 to about 48 in 100 on about 200 pairs; the three block activities fall in lockstep while their internal routing stays stable (A20→A26 about 97 in 100 in both windows); and A15→A26 within five steps appears (1→75 traces). Screening also rules out chance as an explanation of the pattern as a whole: 29 control-flow items qualified against about 0.73 expected without a change, although several items describe the same underlying trace behaviour rather than independent confirmations. [OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, DIR005, DIR008, LAG008, DIR007, LAG007]

The evidence cannot distinguish whether each case can now optionally skip these steps or whether the later window mixes old-style and new-style traces; for A06 specifically, the scattered successors and later positions leave open that it now also occurs in a different context rather than only being bypassed. [POS001, DIR003]

Other differences: A04, A08 and A10 participate more often (about 4–5 in 100 traces before, 15–20 in 100 after); A44→A45 and A46→A47 become slightly less exclusive (96→86 and 97→87 in 100); the outgoing profiles of the rare activities A02, A04 and A08 change, but with about 8–43 observed transitions per window these are weakly based. [OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, DIR009, DIR010, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004]
